summary: A symmetric floating tunable coupler enables fast adiabatic CZ gates between fixed-frequency transmons while maintaining exact residual $ZZ=0$ cancellation at idling, exploiting favorable energy-level ordering that eliminates the traditional trade-off between gate speed and adiabatic evolution. The work demonstrates a 24 ns gate with fidelity $99.919 	ext{ ± } 0.010	ext{ %}$ using adiabatically-weighted pulse shaping based on instantaneous adiabatic factors.
motivation: Prior tunable-coupler architectures faced a fundamental trade-off: achieving large dynamical phase accumulation for fast gates, maintaining favorable energy-level ordering for robust adiabatic evolution, and preserving exact $ZZ=0$ idling were mutually incompatible, especially in non-straddling regimes required for high-speed gates.
method: Two fixed-frequency transmons (Q1, Q2 at 3588, 3686 MHz with anharmonicities $-227, -221$ MHz) are coupled via a symmetric floating coupler idled at $\Phi_{c,\mathrm{dc}} = 0.35\,\Phi_0$ with $ZZ = 27.3$ kHz. Gates use flux pulses with simple Fourier-cosine envelopes or adiabatically-weighted pulses (AWP) that modulate coupler frequency based on computed instantaneous adiabatic factors $D(\omega_c)$, maintaining $\zeta/2\pi$ up to 60 MHz while operating in the straddling regime.
result: Fourier-cosine pulses achieve $>99.5\text{ %}$ iRB fidelity down to 40 ns; AWP extends this to 24 ns with $99.919 \text{ ± } 0.010\text{ %}$ iRB fidelity (peak value), and 8.5-hour stability yields $99.874 \text{ ± } 0.018\text{ %}$ average, with coherence-limited performance from $T_1 \sim 35$ µs and $T_2^* \sim 10$–40 µs in the high-frequency gate regime where $f_c \approx 3.5$ GHz.
